title: Reviewer Bias Spotter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Distinguish the bias shown in each of eight reviewer notes from six named biases and a no-bias option, and learn the defense for each.

learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish the bias shown in each of eight reviewer notes from six named biases and a no-bias option, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The term reviewer bias and the six biases listed in [Chapter 3](../../chapters/03-ten-metric-rubric-scoring/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, commit an answer, and read the reason
keyQuestions: What moved the score: the descriptors or something else?
commonMisconceptions: Anchoring and the halo effect are the same
A confident note shows no bias
assessmentOpportunities: "The graphics are gorgeous, so I gave every metric an 8 or higher." Which bias?
"It comes from a famous university press, so I skipped the link check." Which bias?
How does anchoring differ from the halo effect?
What does a note with no bias look like?

controls.name: Seven option buttons
controls.description: the six biases and No bias. The choice is final.

controls.name: Show bias table
controls.description: opens a table of the six biases, what happens, and the defense. Opening it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Play again** and the missed-note review on the results screen.
